summary: Picks one of two to five views or modes, shown side by side as attached buttons: the brand of a preview, the density, light or dark. The choice applies at once, on the current screen.
whenToUse: Switching how the same content is shown: Light or Dark, Comfortable or Compact, Grid or List.
Two to five short options that fit on one line, where seeing every option at once helps the choice.
The change applies immediately, with no Save button.
Size sm in toolbars, menus and dense panels; md everywhere else. Heights follow the density setting.
fullWidth inside a narrow panel or menu, so the segments share the width equally.
whenNotToUse: Switching between panels of different content: use Tabs, which link each tab to its panel.
A setting in a form that is saved later: use RadioGroup, which shows a label and help per option.
More than five options or long labels: use Select.
Turning one thing on or off: use Switch.
Triggering actions (Export, Delete): use Button or an attached ButtonGroup.

dos.title: Short, parallel labels
dos.text: One or two words per segment, same grammatical form, so the set reads as one choice.

dos.title: Always start with a selection
dos.text: A segmented control shows the current mode. Pass value or defaultValue so one segment is always selected.

donts.title: Actions dressed as segments
donts.text: Segments select a mode; they never run a command. "Export" and "Share" belong on buttons.

donts.title: Too many or too long options
donts.text: Past five segments or two words each, the row wraps or truncates and stops reading as one control. Use Select.

accessibility: Base UI RadioGroup with native button radios: role radiogroup on the row, role radio and aria-checked on each segment.
Tab enters the group on the selected segment and leaves it; arrow keys move the selection, Home and End jump to the ends.
Give the group a name: label, or aria-labelledby pointing at a visible heading.
The selected segment is marked by a raised plate and a darker text color, not by color alone.
The focus ring (focus.ring.color) shows on keyboard focus only.
Rendered without JavaScript, the HTML keeps role, aria-checked and data-value, so a small script can drive it: flip aria-checked and tabindex, and handle arrow keys.
contentGuidelines: Sentence case nouns or adjectives: "Compact", "Dark", "Grid". No verbs: segments are states, not actions.
One or two words. Drop the shared word: "Light, Dark", not "Light theme, Dark theme".
Name the group with what is being chosen: "Density", "Brand", "Themes shown".

anatomy.leading: Decoration before the label, for example a color swatch
anatomy.label: Label
